sentences.text: This petition is filed by the petitioner-accused under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. for quashing the FIR in Crime No.249/2022 registered by Sanjay Nagar Police Station, Bengaluru for the offences punishable under Sections 384, 504, 506, 448, 420, 468, 406 of IPC.
2. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the petitioner, learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1-State and respondent No.2-party-in-person.

3. The case of the petitioner is that on the complaint of respondent No.2, the Police registered the FIR against the petitioner for the above said offences and it is alleged by the complainant that the petitioner and respondent No.2 entered into the lease agreement on 16.02.2012 and he has received Rs.3,75,000/- towards the mortgage period and later, it was repaid to him, but the petitioner wanted to continue as a tenant and he has continued.

Even for improvement of his business he has received Rs.8,50,000/- from the complainant on three dates i.e., on 29.07.2015 for Rs.1,00,000/-,
on 18.08.2015 for Rs.5,00,000/- and on 07.09.2015 for Rs.2,50,000/-.

Later, he NC:
2024:KHC:6781 has neither repaid the loan amount nor vacated the premises.

Even on 31.12.2015,
the petitioner paid Rs.50,000/- towards 10 months rent.
Thereafter, he has not vacated the premises but threatening the complainant to execute the sale deed on the ground that he has to pay Rs.25,00,000/- to him by creating the documents.
Based upon the complaint, the Police registered the FIR, which is under challenge.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has contended that the respondent has taken three contentions in his complaint as well as legal notice which is contrary to his case, where the petitioner and respondent No.2 entered into an agreement in the year 2010.
The petitioner paid Rs.25,00,000/- to the respondent No.2.
The total sale amount is Rs.75,00,000/-.

Therefore, the petitioner staying in the house as agreement holder and this oral agreement was entered into between themselves in the year 2012 as a lease agreement holder, but no such amount was paid by respondent to the petitioner.
On the other hand, the petitioner paid Rs.25,00,000/- to the respondent No.2.
There is no case for investigating the matter.
Hence, prayed for quashing the same.
Per contra, learned High Court Government Pleader objected the same and respondent No.2 also objected the petition and filed written objections.

sentences.text: Having heard the arguments and on perusal of the records, which reveals, of course, there is an agreement said to be entered between the parties in the year 2010 for execution of sale deed.
But the petitioner has not filed any suit for enforcing the agreement of sale for last 14 years.
It is alleged by the complainant that the petitioner took the premises as a mortgagee for Rs.3,75,000/- and thereafter, it was repaid to the petitioner.
Subsequently, the petitioner want to continue the house as a tenant for Rs.5,000/- per month.

Subsequently, the petitioner said to be paid only Rs.50,000/- to the respondent No.2 on 31.12.2015 and subsequently, he got created some document and threatened the complainant to vacate the premises and trying to extract the money.

Considering the fact of the case, though there is some discrepancies in the legal notice issued by the complainant in respect of payment of Rs.3,25,000/- towards the mortgage amount and repaying Rs.50,000/- as advance amount and receiving Rs.50,000/- as rental amount on 31.12.2015 but that NC: 2024:KHC:6781 itself is not a ground to quash the FIR.

If at all, the petitioner staying in the premises as a agreement holder, he can produce the same before the Police for investigation and he can also produce all the documents for payment of Rs.25,00,000/- to the respondent No.2 in order to establish his case, the police after the investigation found there is no cognizance case made out by the petitioner and the police can file 'B' final report.
If the offence is committed by the petitioner, the Police can file charge sheet.
Such being the case, it is not a fit case for quashing the FIR.
Accordingly, the petition is dismissed.
